# package app

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-dnp3/app"
```

Package app is the DNP3 application layer codec (IEEE 1815-2012 clause 4 and Annex A): fragments with their control octet, function code and internal indications, object headers with their qualifiers, and the object library.

A [Fragment](#type-fragment) is a list of [Header](#type-header) values; each header names a group and variation ([GroupVariation](#type-groupvariation)) and carries [Object](#type-object) values, an index plus a [Value](#type-value). The value types are a closed set of structs (for example [Binary](#type-binary), [Analog](#type-analog), [Counter](#type-counter), [CROB](#type-crob), [FileTransport](#type-filetransport), [AuthChallenge](#type-authchallenge)); variations of the same kind of point share one struct and the header's variation decides the encoding.

The library covers every object group of IEEE 1815-2012 Annex A that a current device sends: binary and double-bit inputs, binary outputs and commands, counters and frozen counters, analog inputs, frozen analog inputs, deadbands, analog outputs and commands, time objects, class objects, file control (group 70), internal indications, device attributes (group 0), BCD and small integers, octet strings and virtual terminal objects, and the secure authentication objects (groups 120 to 122). The device storage buffer fill status (g81v1, not recommended for new implementations) is decoded into [BufferFillStatus](#type-bufferfillstatus), and the device profile (g82v1) is carried as [Raw](#type-raw) payload, as are the data set and private registration objects (groups 83 to 91) except the data set characteristics (g86v2, [DataSetCharacteristics](#type-datasetcharacteristics)). Group 100, the obsolete floating-point objects, is not: IEEE 1815-2012 A.38 defines no coding for its variations.

The package is a pure codec: it does no I/O and keeps no state between fragments. It imports nothing outside the standard library.

Standard device attribute variations of group 0 (set 0).

IEEE 1815-2012 Annex A (A.1.1 to A.1.44) defines 209 to 243, 245 to 250, 252, 254 and 255. The variations 196 to 208 and 244 are not defined in IEEE 1815-2012; there, index 0 variations 1 to 253 are pre-assigned or reserved for assignment by the DNP Users Group (5.5.2).

## Variables

```go
var (
	// ErrMalformed reports a fragment that cannot be parsed: too short,
	// a count or range that does not fit the remaining octets, or a field
	// with a value the object does not allow.
	ErrMalformed = errors.New("app: malformed fragment")

	// ErrUnknownObject reports a group and variation this package does not
	// know, in a position where its size must be known to continue.
	ErrUnknownObject = errors.New("app: unknown object")

	// ErrInvalidQualifier reports a qualifier code that is reserved or not
	// allowed for the object.
	ErrInvalidQualifier = errors.New("app: invalid qualifier")

	// ErrInvalidValue reports a header or object that cannot be encoded:
	// a value of the wrong type for the variation, indexes that do not fit
	// the qualifier, or a field that is too long.
	ErrInvalidValue = errors.New("app: invalid value")
)
```

Errors returned by [Decode](#func-decode) and the encoders. They are wrapped with detail; test with errors.Is.

An outstation answers a request that fails with ErrUnknownObject with IIN2.1 (OBJECT\_UNKNOWN) and one that fails with ErrMalformed or ErrInvalidQualifier with IIN2.2 (PARAMETER\_ERROR).

```go
var ErrUnknownFunction = errors.New("app: unknown function code")
```

ErrUnknownFunction reports a fragment whose function code IEEE 1815-2012 does not define. [Decode](#func-decode) returns the header of such a fragment with it, so that an outstation can answer with IIN2.0 (NO\_FUNC\_CODE\_SUPPORT).

## Functions

### func AppendFileDescriptor

```go
func AppendFileDescriptor(b []byte, d FileDescriptor) ([]byte, error)
```

AppendFileDescriptor appends the encoding of one file descriptor object (without object header), the form in which a directory's entries are transferred as the content of the directory file.

### func AppendObjectValue

```go
func AppendObjectValue(b []byte, gv GroupVariation, v Value) ([]byte, error)
```

AppendObjectValue appends the encoding of one object of gv without any header, prefix or size: the octets a free-format object carries. Secure authentication uses it to reproduce an object exactly, for example the key status message of a session key change. Relative-time variations are not supported: they need the CTO of their fragment.

### func IINBit

```go
func IINBit(bit IIN) uint32
```

IINBit returns the index of a single IIN bit in the numbering of group 80 (IIN1.0 is 0, IIN2.7 is 15), the index a master writes to clear it.

### func NextSeq


NextSeq returns the sequence number that follows seq, modulo 16.

```go

	Delay time.Duration

```

ActivateConfigStatus is the content of a status of requested operation object (g91v1): the outstation's answer to ACTIVATE\_CONFIG. [Decode](#func-decode) returns g91v1 objects as [Raw](#type-raw); [ParseActivateConfigStatus](#func-parseactivateconfigstatus) reads their data and [ActivateConfigStatus.Raw](#func-activateconfigstatus-raw) makes one.

#### func ParseActivateConfigStatus

```go
func ParseActivateConfigStatus(data []byte) (ActivateConfigStatus, error)
```

ParseActivateConfigStatus reads the data of one g91v1 object (the Data of the [Raw](#type-raw) that [Decode](#func-decode) returns). It fails with ErrMalformed when the data are not exactly one status of requested operation.

#### func (ActivateConfigStatus) Raw

```go
func (s ActivateConfigStatus) Raw() (Raw, error)
```

Raw encodes s as the data of a g91v1 object, to send for example as app.Counted(app.G91V1, raw). It fails with ErrInvalidValue when Delay is negative or does not fit 32 bits of milliseconds, when there are more than 255 results, or when a text is longer than 254 octets.

```go
}
```

Analog is an analog input (group 30), a frozen analog input (group 31), an analog output status (group 40) or an event of one of these (groups 32, 33 and 42).

Encoding a value into an integer variation rounds it to the nearest integer; a value the variation cannot hold is sent as the nearest value it can, with FlagOverRange set in the variations with flags.

### type BCD

```go
type BCD struct {
	Value uint64
	// Negative marks a negative number; Value is its magnitude.
	Negative bool
}
```

BCD is a binary-coded decimal integer (group 101): 4 digits (v1), 8 digits (v2) or 16 digits (v3). Value is the magnitude of the decimal number and Negative its sign.

A negative value carries its sign in the most significant BCD character, so it has one digit fewer: BCDn holds -(10^(n-1)-1) to 10^n-1 (IEEE 1815-2012 11.3.6.1, Table 11-2, and 11.3.6.2). On receipt any of the characters 0xA..0xF in that position marks a negative value; this package sends 0xF, as the standard does not name one. A negative zero is sent, and decoded, as zero.

```go
	Flags Flags
```

### type Flags

```go
type Flags uint8
```

Flags is the quality flags octet of a point (IEEE 1815-2012 11.6.1, Table 11-5).

The state bits that share the octet with the flags of binary and double-bit points (bit 7, bits 6..7) are not part of Flags: they are the Value of [Binary](#type-binary) and [DoubleBitBinary](#type-doublebitbinary), merged on encoding.

```go
const (
	// FlagOnline: the point is available and its value is valid.
	FlagOnline Flags = 0x01
	// FlagRestart: the value has not been updated since the device
	// restarted.
	FlagRestart Flags = 0x02
	// FlagCommLost: the value was obtained from a device that has lost
	// communication.
	FlagCommLost Flags = 0x04
	// FlagRemoteForced: the value is forced at a downstream device.
	FlagRemoteForced Flags = 0x08
	// FlagLocalForced: the value is forced at this device.
	FlagLocalForced Flags = 0x10
)
```

Flag bits common to all point types.

```go
const (
	// FlagChatterFilter: binary and double-bit inputs; the input is
	// changing too fast and is filtered.
	FlagChatterFilter Flags = 0x20
	// FlagRollover: counters; obsolete. Outstations shall not set it and
	// masters shall ignore it (IEEE 1815-2012 Table 11-5).
	FlagRollover Flags = 0x20
	// FlagOverRange: analog inputs and outputs; the value exceeds the
	// range of the variation or of the device.
	FlagOverRange Flags = 0x20
	// FlagDiscontinuity: counters; the value cannot be compared with the
	// previous one.
	FlagDiscontinuity Flags = 0x40
	// FlagReferenceErr: analog inputs, analog output status and analog
	// output events; the value might not have the expected accuracy, for
	// example because the reference signal is in error.
	FlagReferenceErr Flags = 0x40
)
```

Flag bits specific to some point types.

#### func (Flags) String

```go
func (f Flags) String() string
```

String returns the common flags by name and the type-specific bits as "BIT5"/"BIT6", for example "ONLINE|BIT5".

### type Fragment

```go
type Fragment struct {
	Control  Control
	Function FunctionCode
	// IIN are the internal indications; only responses carry them.
	IIN     IIN
	Headers []Header
}
```

Fragment is one application layer fragment: the request or response header and the object headers.

#### func Decode

```go
func Decode(b []byte) (*Fragment, error)
```

Decode decodes one fragment. The objects are copies: nothing in the result aliases b.

On error the returned fragment is still non-nil when b held the fragment header, with the headers decoded before the failure, so that an outstation can answer with the sequence number and function of the request. Errors wrap ErrMalformed, ErrUnknownObject, ErrInvalidQualifier or ErrUnknownFunction.

#### func (Fragment) AppendEncode

```go
func (f *Fragment) AppendEncode(b []byte) ([]byte, error)
```

AppendEncode appends the wire encoding of f to b.

A response (function 129..131) cannot carry a header with qualifier 0x06 (ErrInvalidQualifier), nor one of group 60 or of a request-only variation such as variation 0 (ErrInvalidValue): IEEE 1815-2012 Table 4-8, 4.2.2.7.1.1 and 4.2.2.7.2.1. [Decode](#func-decode) refuses them in a response too.

#### func (Fragment) Encode

```go
func (f *Fragment) Encode() ([]byte, error)
```

Encode returns the wire encoding of f.

#### func (Fragment) HeaderLen

```go
func (f *Fragment) HeaderLen() int
```

HeaderLen returns the size of the fragment header: 2 for a request, 4 for a response.

#### func (Fragment) String

```go
func (f *Fragment) String() string
```

String returns a one-line description, for example "RESPONSE FIR FIN seq=3 iin=DEVICE\_RESTART headers=2".

### type Header

```go
type Header struct {
	GV        GroupVariation
	Qualifier Qualifier

	// Start and Stop are the range of a start-stop qualifier. When the
	// header has objects, the encoder takes the range from their indexes.
	Start, Stop uint32

	// Count is the count of a count, index-prefixed or free-format
	// qualifier for a header without objects, for example a READ of at
	// most Count events. With objects the encoder uses len(Objects).
	Count uint32

	// Objects is nil for a header that names points without values: the
	// headers of READ, freeze, assign class and unsolicited control
	// requests. When such a header names points by an index list (an
	// index-prefixed qualifier such as 0x17 or 0x28), Objects holds the
	// indexes with a nil Value.
	Objects []Object
}
```

Header is one object header and the objects that follow it.

#### func AllObjects

```go
func AllObjects(gv GroupVariation) Header
```

AllObjects returns a header for all objects of gv (qualifier 0x06), for example the class 0 header of an integrity poll.

#### func ClassHeaders

```go
func ClassHeaders(classes ...int) []Header
```

ClassHeaders returns the headers that read the given classes (0..3), in the order given: ClassHeaders(1, 2, 3, 0) is an integrity poll.

#### func CountOf

```go
func CountOf(gv GroupVariation, n uint32) Header
```

CountOf returns a header naming up to n objects of gv without values, as in a READ of at most n events.

#### func Counted

```go
func Counted(gv GroupVariation, values ...Value) Header
```

Counted returns a header carrying objects without index (qualifier 0x07..0x09), as used for time objects: Counted(G50V1, AbsoluteTime{...}).

#### func FreeFormat

```go
func FreeFormat(gv GroupVariation, values ...Value) Header
```

FreeFormat returns a header carrying free-format objects, each preceded by a two-octet size (qualifier 0x5B), as used for file and authentication objects.

#### func IndexList

```go
func IndexList(gv GroupVariation, indexes ...uint32) Header
```

IndexList returns a header naming the given indexes of gv without values (an index-prefixed qualifier, see [IndexQualifier](#func-indexqualifier)), as in a READ of specific points.

#### func IndexRange

```go
func IndexRange(gv GroupVariation, start, stop uint32) Header
```

IndexRange returns a header naming the points start..stop of gv without values, as in a READ of a range.

#### func Indexed

```go
func Indexed(gv GroupVariation, objs ...Object) Header
```

Indexed returns a header carrying objects each preceded by its index (an index-prefixed qualifier, see [IndexQualifier](#func-indexqualifier)), as used for commands and events.

#### func Ranged

```go
func Ranged(gv GroupVariation, start uint32, values ...Value) Header
```

Ranged returns a header carrying values for the contiguous indexes start, start+1, ... (a start-stop qualifier).

#### func (Header) EncodedLen

```go
func (h *Header) EncodedLen() (int, error)
```

EncodedLen returns the size of the encoding of h on its own, or an error when it cannot be encoded. A server uses it to decide whether a header still fits a fragment.

#### func (Header) String

```go
func (h *Header) String() string
```

String returns a one-line description, for example "g30v1 q=0x00 \[0..9] n=10".

### type IIN

```go
type IIN uint16
```

IIN is the internal indications field of a response (IEEE 1815-2012 clause 4.2.2.6): IIN1 in the low octet, IIN2 in the high octet, as they are sent.

```go
const (
	// IINBroadcast: a broadcast message was received.
	IINBroadcast IIN = 1 << iota
	// IINClass1Events: the outstation has unreported class 1 events.
	IINClass1Events
	// IINClass2Events: the outstation has unreported class 2 events.
	IINClass2Events
	// IINClass3Events: the outstation has unreported class 3 events.
	IINClass3Events
	// IINNeedTime: the outstation requires time synchronization.
	IINNeedTime
	// IINLocalControl: one or more output points are in local mode.
	IINLocalControl
	// IINDeviceTrouble: an abnormal, device specific condition exists.
	IINDeviceTrouble
	// IINDeviceRestart: the outstation restarted; cleared by the master.
	IINDeviceRestart

	// IIN2 bits.

	// IINNoFuncCodeSupport: the function code is not implemented.
	IINNoFuncCodeSupport
	// IINObjectUnknown: an object, variation or qualifier is not supported,
	// or a point does not exist.
	IINObjectUnknown
	// IINParameterError: a parameter in the request is invalid, or the
	// request could not be parsed.
	IINParameterError
	// IINEventBufferOverflow: an event buffer overflowed and events were
	// lost.
	IINEventBufferOverflow
	// IINAlreadyExecuting: the requested operation is already executing.
	IINAlreadyExecuting
	// IINConfigCorrupt: the outstation detected corrupt configuration.
	IINConfigCorrupt
	// IINReserved2 and IINReserved1 are reserved; they are sent as zero.
	IINReserved2
	IINReserved1
)
```

IIN1 bits.

### type Qualifier

```go
type Qualifier uint8
```

Qualifier is the qualifier octet of an object header (IEEE 1815-2012 clause 4.2.2.7.3): the object prefix code in bits 4..6 and the range specifier code in bits 0..3.

```go
const (
	// Range of indexes, objects in index order.
	Qual1ByteStartStop Qualifier = 0x00
	Qual2ByteStartStop Qualifier = 0x01
	Qual4ByteStartStop Qualifier = 0x02

	// Range of virtual addresses (device attributes and similar).
	Qual1ByteVirtualStartStop Qualifier = 0x03
	Qual2ByteVirtualStartStop Qualifier = 0x04
	Qual4ByteVirtualStartStop Qualifier = 0x05

	// All objects of the group and variation; no range field.
	QualAll Qualifier = 0x06

	// A count of objects, without index.
	Qual1ByteCount Qualifier = 0x07
	Qual2ByteCount Qualifier = 0x08
	Qual4ByteCount Qualifier = 0x09

	// A count of objects, each preceded by its index.
	Qual1ByteIndexCount Qualifier = 0x17
	Qual2ByteIndexCount Qualifier = 0x28
	Qual4ByteIndexCount Qualifier = 0x39

	// A one-octet count of free-format objects, each preceded by its size.
	Qual1ByteSizeFreeFormat Qualifier = 0x4B
	Qual2ByteSizeFreeFormat Qualifier = 0x5B
	Qual4ByteSizeFreeFormat Qualifier = 0x6B
)
```

The qualifiers in use. The name gives the prefix and the range: for example Qual2ByteIndexCount is "prefix: 2-octet index, range: 2-octet count" (0x28).

#### func CountQualifier

```go
func CountQualifier(n int) Qualifier
```

CountQualifier returns the smallest count qualifier that holds n.

#### func IndexQualifier

```go
func IndexQualifier(n int, maxIndex uint32) Qualifier
```

IndexQualifier returns the index-prefixed count qualifier for n objects with indexes up to maxIndex.

While the count and the indexes fit two octets it is one of the preferred codes (IEEE 1815-2012 Table 4-7): 0x17 when both fit one octet, else 0x28. Beyond that the index takes four octets only when maxIndex needs them, and the count the fewest octets that hold n, because four-octet indexes should not be used below 65 536 points and four-octet counts should be avoided (4.2.2.7.3.4): 0x29 for more than 65 535 objects with two-octet indexes, and 0x37, 0x38 or 0x39 with four-octet indexes.

#### func RangeQualifier

```go
func RangeQualifier(stop uint32) Qualifier
```

RangeQualifier returns the smallest start-stop qualifier that holds stop.

```go
}
```

TimeDelay is a time delay object (group 52): coarse (v1, seconds) or fine (v2, milliseconds).

### type Timestamp

```go
type Timestamp uint64
```

Timestamp is DNP3 absolute time: milliseconds since 1970-01-01 00:00 UTC, 48 bits on the wire (DNP3TIME, IEEE 1815-2012 clause 3 and 10.3.2; a UINT48 by Table 11-4).

It is carried as the integer the standard defines rather than as a time.Time so that values round-trip exactly; [Timestamp.Time](#func-timestamp-time) and [TimestampOf](#func-timestampof) convert.

```go
const MaxTimestamp Timestamp = 1<<48 - 1
```

MaxTimestamp is the largest value 48 bits hold.

#### func Now

```go
func Now() Timestamp
```

Now returns the current time as a Timestamp.

#### func TimestampOf

```go
func TimestampOf(t time.Time) Timestamp
```

TimestampOf returns the timestamp of t, truncated to milliseconds and clamped to 0..MaxTimestamp.

#### func (Timestamp) String

```go
func (t Timestamp) String() string
```

String formats the timestamp in RFC 3339 with milliseconds.

#### func (Timestamp) Time

```go
func (t Timestamp) Time() time.Time
```

Time returns the timestamp as a time.Time in UTC.

### type TripClose

```go
type TripClose uint8
```

TripClose is the trip-close code of a control relay output block.

```go
const (
	TCCNul   TripClose = 0
	TCCClose TripClose = 1
	TCCTrip  TripClose = 2
)
```

Trip-close codes.

#### func (TripClose) String

```go
func (t TripClose) String() string
```

String returns "NUL", "CLOSE", "TRIP" or "TCC(n)".

### type UnsignedInteger

```go
type UnsignedInteger struct {
	Value uint8
}
```

UnsignedInteger is an unsigned 8-bit integer (g102v1).

### type Value

```go
type Value interface {
	// contains filtered or unexported methods
}
```

Value is one decoded object: the value of a point, a command, a time object, a file or authentication object.

The set of implementations is closed: it is the value structs of this package, used by value. Several variations share a struct; the variation the object is sent in is that of its [Header](#type-header). Use a type switch to consume them:

	for _, o := range h.Objects {
		switch v := o.Value.(type) {
		case app.Analog:
			...
		case app.Binary:
			...
		}
	}
